fixes.explanation: True, friend. After the punishment is laid out, the text adds, "…whether man or beast, he must not live." (Exodus 19:13) So the boundary around the mountain isn't only for people. Man or beast, the same rule applies. Even somebody's goat has to keep its hooves off.

That's the one, friend. The text says, "Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke, because the LORD had descended on it in fire." (Exodus 19:18) The smoke comes from the LORD coming down. I've had smoke in my bakery before, but that was just a forgotten batch, and all anybody did was open the windows.

True, friend. The LORD has just called Moses to the summit, and Moses goes up (Exodus 19:20). Then the LORD says to him, "Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) Up the mountain, then right back down again. I bet his legs have opinions.

Nice try, friend, but Paran isn't the name in this passage. The text says Israel set out from Rephidim and entered the Wilderness of Sinai, and camped there in front of the mountain (Exodus 19:2). That's a lot of desert names to juggle, and I'd mix them up too. Hold onto Sinai.

A campfire is a cozy picture, but it isn't the one the text uses. It says, "…the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace…" (Exodus 19:18) The comparison is a furnace, friend. Save the campfire for another night.

It does happen, friend. Once Moses has gone up, the LORD says to him, "Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) That's the instruction Moses gets at the summit. So True is the answer. Up the mountain, then straight back down with a warning.
